findings_addressed.oracle: Two real bridge snapshots (before and after tab refresh) form a union set; every rendered PID must be a member of that union. Additionally, all rendered PIDs must be non-negative integers (structural oracle). Together these prove the rendered set is derived from genuine list_processes_detailed enumeration, not fabricated data.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In ProcessBridge._iterate_process_snapshot_detailed (process.py), change `results.append({...})` to instead append a dict with `'pid': entry.th32ProcessID + 9_000_000` — a fabricated PID range far outside any real OS PID space — and the `assert not spurious` assertion will fail because those invented PIDs appear in neither snapshot.

notes: Finding G0019 was a weak-existence check: the test only asserted os.getpid() appeared in both the bridge snapshot and the rendered set (N8 - existence check), but never enforced the documented subset relationship. The hardened test takes two bridge snapshots (before and after the tab refresh) to form a churn-tolerant union, then asserts: (1) all rendered PIDs are positive integers, (2) own PID appears in rendered set, and (3) rendered PIDs are a subset of the union. A production implementation that fabricated arbitrary PIDs would fail assertion (3) immediately. The pids_before/pids_after set comprehensions use int() cast to satisfy basedpyright (bridge return type is dict[str, int | str | float]). POST-WORKFLOW FIX (2026-06-22): the structural oracle originally required `pid > 0`, which failed in the sandbox because list_processes_detailed legitimately enumerates PID 0 (the Windows System Idle Process, confirmed present on host: 302 procs, non-positive pids=[0]). Relaxed to `pid >= 0` (Windows PIDs are non-negative); still rejects fabricated str/None/negative payloads. Verified GREEN in sandbox.
